questions.q: ______ is called as “Father of Indian Green Revolution”.
questions.solution:
**M.S. Swaminathan** is called the Father of the Indian Green Revolution. He introduced high-yielding semi-dwarf wheat and rice varieties in the 1960s.

P. Maheshwari was an embryologist, Mendel the father of genetics, and Nel Jayaraman a Tamil Nadu conserver of traditional rice varieties.

**Tephrosia purpurea** (kolinji) is a **green manure** crop: a legume grown and ploughed into the soil to add organic matter and nitrogen.

Other green manures named in the textbook include Crotalaria juncea (sunn hemp) and Sesbania.

questions.q:
Assertion (A) : Gamma rays are generally used to induce mutation in wheat varieties.
Reason (R) : Because they carry lower energy to non-ionize electrons from atom.
questions.solution:
The **assertion is correct**: gamma rays are widely used to induce mutations in crops such as wheat.

The **reason is wrong**: gamma rays are **high-energy, ionising** radiation that knock electrons out of atoms; that is exactly why they cause mutations.

questions.q:
Match the following :
Column - I | Column - II
(1) Cowpea | (i) Pusa Sadabahar
(2) Wheat | (ii) Pusa Swarnim
(3) Chilli | (iii) Himgiri
(4) Brassica | (iv) Pusa Komal
questions.solution:
Correct matches:

Cowpea — **Pusa Komal** (bacterial blight resistant)
Wheat — **Himgiri** (resistant to leaf and stripe rust, hill bunt)
Chilli — **Pusa Sadabahar** (resistant to chilly mosaic virus, leaf curl)
Brassica — **Pusa Swarnim** (white rust resistant)

So (1)-(iv), (2)-(iii), (3)-(i), (4)-(ii).

questions.q: The superiority of an F₁ hybrid over both its parents is called:
questions.solution:
**Heterosis** (hybrid vigour) is the superiority of the F₁ in yield, size or vigour over its parents. The term was coined by Shull.

Inbreeding depression is the opposite: loss of vigour after repeated self-pollination.

questions.q: Azolla is used as a biofertilizer in paddy fields because it harbours the nitrogen-fixing cyanobacterium:
questions.solution:
The water fern **Azolla** carries **Anabaena azollae** in its leaf cavities; the cyanobacterium fixes atmospheric nitrogen that enriches the paddy field.

Rhizobium lives in legume root nodules and Azotobacter is free-living in soil.

questions.q: Sonalika and Kalyan Sona are high-yielding varieties of:
questions.solution:
**Sonalika** and **Kalyan Sona** are semi-dwarf, high-yielding, disease-resistant **wheat** varieties developed from Mexican wheat during the Green Revolution.

The rice counterparts were IR-8, Jaya and Padma.

questions.q: Clonal selection is used in crops that are:
questions.solution:
**Clonal selection** picks the best plants from a mixed population of a **vegetatively propagated** crop (banana, potato, sugarcane) and multiplies them as clones.

The clone is genetically identical to its parent, so the selected quality is kept.

questions.q: Atlas 66, used as a donor for improving wheat, is rich in:
questions.solution:
**Atlas 66**, a wheat variety with high **protein** content, was used as the donor to breed protein-rich cultivated wheat: an example of biofortification.

Biofortification breeds crops for higher vitamins, minerals, protein or healthier oils.

questions.q: In a double cross, (A × B) × (C × D), how many inbred parents are involved?
questions.solution:
**4** parents: two single crosses, A × B and C × D, are made first and their F₁s are then crossed with each other.

Double crosses were used in maize to produce hybrid seed economically.

questions.q: Name the radioactive isotope commonly used as a source of gamma rays in mutation breeding.
questions.solution:
**Cobalt-60** ($^{60}\mathrm{Co}$) is the usual gamma source; caesium-137 is also used.

Seeds or plant parts are exposed in a gamma garden or gamma cell, and the useful mutants are selected from the following generations.

questions.q: What is the progeny of a single self-pollinated homozygous plant called?
questions.solution:
It is a **pure line**. All its plants are homozygous and genetically alike, so it breeds true.

Pure line selection, based on Johannsen's work, is used to improve self-pollinated crops such as wheat and rice.

questions.q: The rice variety IR-8 was developed at the International Rice Research Institute. In which country is that institute?
questions.solution:
IRRI is at Los Baños in the **Philippines**. IR-8, a semi-dwarf 'miracle rice', was released in 1966.

In India it was used with Taichung Native-1 from Taiwan to develop Jaya and Padma.

questions.q: Name the bacterial genus that fixes nitrogen in the root nodules of leguminous plants.
questions.solution:
**Rhizobium**. It infects legume roots, forms nodules and fixes atmospheric nitrogen into ammonia using the enzyme nitrogenase.

Rhizobium cultures are applied to legume seeds as a biofertilizer before sowing.

questions.q: What is single cell protein ? Mention its applications.
questions.solution:
Model answer:

**Single cell protein (SCP)** is protein obtained from the dried cells of micro-organisms such as algae (Spirulina, Chlorella), yeast (Saccharomyces), fungi and bacteria, grown on cheap substrates and used as food or feed. Spirulina, for example, can be grown on waste water from potato processing, straw, molasses, animal manure and sewage.

**Applications:**

1. A rich source of **protein** (Spirulina has about 60–70%), with vitamins, minerals and essential amino acids; used against malnutrition.

2. Used as **animal and poultry feed** and in fish farming.

3. Used in **health foods** and as food supplements, including for astronauts.

4. Micro-organisms grow very fast, need little land and water, and can be grown on **waste materials**, which also reduces environmental pollution.

5. Used in cosmetics and as a source of pigments and natural colours.
